catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class binds a waveform capture on an instrument: cap.sensing.read.v1 declares sensor, sensor.imu and sensor.force_torque; cap.measure.voltage.v1 declares instrument.dmm, instrument.smu and sensor; cap.sensing.image.v1 declares sensor.camera. This action returns per-channel scalar measurements from one capture, not the sample arrays.

No catalogue class sets an oscilloscope input range from a min/max mV pair and returns the applied resolution read back from the device; cap.device.configure.v1 is a named-parameter write and cannot carry the pair plus the resolution read-back.
No catalogue class enables or disables a DDS signal-generator output; cap.device.configure.v1 is a named-parameter write and the catalogue has no generator-output class.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/gridinwork__ai-oscilloscope-isds205b --backend fake; the evidence is contract_checked and never an MHS-Device level. No hardware was attached, the hardware backend was never opened, and the upstream package was neither installed nor imported. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's helper hint is PythonObjectDriver, but this package is a direct Driver over instrustar.device:Scope with a native.py factory (the card's decision is already direct-driver). The capture action computes Vmin/Vmax/Vpp/Vavg/Vrms from the returned arrays and the input-range action reads the voltage resolution back after the range request; the family result map projects native return members and cannot express that computation. The interface also needs an @estop, a read/write pair over the same state field and three extension actions with inline schemas. Recon: the entry symbol instrustar.device:Scope exists at instrustar/device.py:154 (card line 154, ast). Covered reads: availability, sample rate, ch1/ch2 voltage resolution, ch1/ch2 coupling read-back, DDS output state, memory length and the has_hard_trigger/has_dds/has_io/has_pretrigger_percent/has_roll_mode support flags. Covered writes: the five-rate sample rate, the DDS waveform style, trigger mode/style/source/level/pre-trigger percentage. Covered actions: one capture with per-channel scalar measurements, one input-range request with the applied-resolution read-back, and the DDS output enable. The e-stop disables the DDS output (Scope.generator_enable(False)); no independent hardware e-stop is documented in the clone, and the package is R1 (the card floor), so SAFE-045 is not applicable. NOT COVERED: the captured sample arrays. The standard has no waveform-array capability class, so the package serves the scalar measurements and settings of the oscilloscope, not the samples. A real capture returns actual_kb * 1024 samples per channel (instrustar/device.py:306-313; docs/ISDS205B_PROTOCOL.md:60); the fake returns four placeholder samples per channel to keep the receipts small. Also not covered: the coupling write (the clone documents AC coupling as a non-functional no-op on this unit), the DDS frequency and duty-cycle writes (the clone states no unit or bound and has no getter), roll mode, the pulse-width and hysteresis trigger fields, and the GUI/HTTP API/snapshot code. The sample rate and the waveform/mode/style/source enums are sourced limits; the trigger level and the set_input_range min/max are Limit.operator_required and are refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until site-limits.json supplies them. site-limits.example.json is an example operator overlay, not a statement about any unit, and it may only narrow. The trigger writes report the last value written because the upstream wrapper has no trigger read-back. The fake is an in-memory stand-in, not a transcript; every number in fake.py is placeholder test data and none is copied into a Fact, a Limit or a reference. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); at R1 the loader does not require a reviewed_by signature, so the hardware backend remains an operator decision, and no human review or hardware run is claimed. The hardware path is Windows x64 only because the upstream loads instrustar/bin/vdso_x64.dll with ctypes.WinDLL despite the card's install platform any. Residual risk: instrustar/device.py:155 says Scope is not thread-safe, while the runtime may call the @estop from another thread during a capture; on hardware a human should review that access pattern, which the fake gate cannot exercise. The gate reported no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings.
